To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the medullary MRF is organized so that medial and lateral MFR activate hindlimb MNs with differential predominance and that this activation is mediated in part by dCINs.
the neonatal mouse MRF activates MNs in the lumbar enlargement through a polysynaptic pathway that is mediated in part by dCINs.
(1) dCINs are polysynaptically activated by MRF neurons, and (2) the MRF activates two distinct populations of dCIN, each of which can activate hindlimb MNs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how spinal cord circuits are organized to control movement in the developing mouse.
the organization of functional synaptic connections between the reticular formation (RF) of the brainstem and the spinal cord.
the organization of functional connections between medullary reticulo-spinal neurons and descending commissural inter-neurons in the neonatal mouse spinal cord.

the reticulospinals of the medial and lateral medulla are connected with a number of descending commissural inter-neurons in the lumbar cord of the neonatal mice.
